subject: human intestine
title: Your Gut's Inner Surface Isn't a Tennis Court. It's Much Smaller

scenes.text: Textbooks said your gut's lining would cover a tennis court. They were wrong.
The old figure was one hundred eighty to three hundred square meters, counting all the tiny folds.
In 2014, Swedish scientists measured it properly, down to the microscopic folds.
Your whole digestive tract comes to about thirty-two square meters. Most of it is the small intestine.
That's about half a badminton court, or a small studio apartment.
Still huge for a tube inside you. Just not a tennis court.

description:
For decades, textbooks said the inner surface of the human gut was 180-300 square metres, as big as a tennis court.
In 2014, researchers at the University of Gothenburg (Helander and Fändriks) measured it again and found the whole digestive tract averages about 32 square metres, roughly half a badminton court. The large intestine accounts for only about 2 square metres.
What other textbook fact do you think is wrong?
first_comment: The large intestine is only about 2 square meters of that. What body fact did school get wrong for you?
